text:
carla: FYI we have an invoice from BrightApps LLC (US) that charged NY state sales tax but Sales says the customer is a reseller with a NY resale certificate on file. Can tax confirm what we need to release payment?

carla: Invoice snippet:
```
INV-2026-309
Vendor: BrightApps LLC, EIN 12-3456789
Customer: ResaleCo Inc (NY)
Net: $25,000
Sales tax (8.875% NY): $2,218.75
Total: $27,218.75
```

mike: Sales confirms PO references ResaleCo and they provided a resale certificate during onboarding but vendor didn't apply exemption. @lina-sales attaching the certificate copy.

lina-sales: Attached: ResaleCo_ST120_signed.pdf (NY ST-120 equivalent). It lists ResaleCo EIN and seller as BrightApps LLC. We scanned and uploaded to the CRM.

invoicebot: INV-2026-309 uploaded to NetSuite. Hold code: SALES_TAX_MISMATCH.

sarah: Tax team: For state-level resale exemptions we need a few things before finance can net the tax: (1) a copy of the purchaser's valid resale certificate (signed) that covers the sale, (2) certificate must list the seller name or be otherwise acceptable to the NY Dept of Taxation, (3) the goods/services sold must be the type exempt for resale under NY rules (software subscriptions are sometimes taxable unless resold). We also need to confirm the invoice references the purchaser and PO and that the seller accepts the certificate.

carla: Vendor says they require a seller-facing certificate with their name exactly as on their tax registration. Tom, can you confirm you accept the ST-120 copy and will reissue invoice without tax?

tom-vendor: Hi all 99Tom from BrightApps. We received the ST-120 but our accounting needs the certificate to explicitly name "BrightApps LLC" as the seller. The copy Lina uploaded lists our DBA "BrightApps Services". We can reissue if you resend a certificate naming "BrightApps LLC" exactly or provide a short seller authorization email from ResaleCo confirming the DBA is acceptable. Otherwise our compliance forces us to collect tax.

mike: ResaleCo can sign an amended certificate. @lina-sales can you ask the customer to provide either (A) corrected certificate naming BrightApps LLC, or (B) email confirmation that the DBA is acceptable?

lina-sales: I'll ask now. ETA from customer ~24h. They asked whether finance can pay net now and let vendor credit back tax later.

carla: Finance prefers a corrected certificate before releasing net payment. If customer provides an emailed authorization naming seller name variant we'll accept that for audit if the email is signed by an authorized rep and references the original certificate.

sarah: Also note: if BrightApps reissues a 0% tax invoice with a reference to the resale certificate (certificate # or date) and the customer signs an email confirming DBA equivalence, that'll be sufficient for our NY tax audit file. We'll store both documents.

tom-vendor: Understood. We'll hold payment until reissued invoice received. If reseller can't provide amended cert, is there a process to refund the tax later?

carla: If vendor invoiced tax and we pay it, the purchaser (ResaleCo) may apply for a refund from NY state or BrightApps could issue a credit. That route is messy. Please ask ResaleCo for the corrected docs to speed things up.

invoicebot: Payment hold on INV-2026-309: SALES_TAX_MISMATCH.

lina-sales: Customer replied: they'll send amended certificate with seller name "BrightApps LLC" and a brief confirmation email within 18 hours. I'll update thread when received.

carla: Thanks. Finance action: hold payment until corrected cert + reissued invoice or signed email acceptance arrives. Tax: when docs arrive, please confirm and instruct NetSuite coding for exempt transaction.

sarah: Will do 99pls forward docs to tax@redwood.com.
